name: saas_cloner
description: Clone a SaaS product (Instagram, Twitter, Airbnb, Stripe, etc.) — full-stack with auth, database, and core features.
steps: Identify which product is being cloned and its 3 CORE features (not everything)
Choose stack: React frontend + FastAPI backend (default) or Next.js + Express
Design database schema — identify main entities (User, Post, Like, Follow, etc.)
Build backend: auth (JWT), core models, CRUD routes, file uploads if needed
Build frontend: auth flow (login/register), core feed/listing page, key user actions
Wire frontend API client to backend
Add responsive CSS (Tailwind) — match the aesthetic of the original
Run backend, verify auth works, verify core CRUD works
Run frontend build, verify no errors
Write root README.md: what it is, how to run both apps
best_practices: Focus on 3 core features — not everything. A great MVP beats a broken full clone.
Start with auth — every SaaS clone needs it and everything else depends on it
Use fake/seed data to pre-populate the app so it looks alive immediately
For image-heavy clones (Instagram): use URLs for images, not actual file uploads (simpler)
Pagination is required for feed-style apps — implement it from the start
Add loading skeletons on the frontend for async data fetching
Never store passwords in plaintext — always bcrypt
README must explain how to start both the backend and frontend
system_prompt_injection: You are building a SaaS clone. Focus on the 3 CORE features that define the product — build them completely and correctly. Create ALL files. Use React + FastAPI + SQLite unless told otherwise. Build backend first (auth + data models + routes), then frontend (auth flow + core UI + API integration). After all files are created, run both apps to verify they start. Fix any errors. The clone must be functional — not just scaffolding.
